claims.text: Perfectly equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi nanoalloys have maximal lattice distortion.
Maximal lattice distortion creates a complex energy landscape for atomic motion.
The distortion-induced energy landscape retards atomic diffusion at high temperature.
Retarded atomic diffusion inhibits phase separation and stabilizes the single-phase structure.
A ±10% imbalance in one component of CoCrFeMnNi reduces lattice distortion relative to the equiatomic alloy.
Reduced lattice distortion lowers barriers to atomic movement and increases elemental diffusion.
Enhanced elemental diffusion increases segregation and nanoscale precipitate formation.
After inert-atmosphere annealing at 750–1000 °C for 1–10 hours, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi nanoalloys will remain single phase with minimal elemental segregation.
Under the same annealing conditions, off-equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi nanoalloys will exhibit phase separation, compositional segregation, or nanoscale precipitates earlier than the equiatomic baseline.
